newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds tax break for French post office.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds tax break for French post office.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance upheld on Thursday the French government's right to give a tax break to the state post office.

The CFI, turning down an appeal by five French insurance groups, said the tax advantage was acceptable under European Union rules on state aid since it helped the post office fulfil its public service obligations.
The insurance groups challenged a 1990 law authorising the post office, La Poste, to offer insurance services and granting it a reduced rate for paying local taxes.
They argued that the concession allowed the post office to "cross-subsidise" its insurance activities.

The court supported the European Commission, which found that the tax concession was less than the economic burden of La Poste's public-interest tasks, such as the obligation to operate post offices in unprofitable rural areas.

Article 90(2) of the EC Treaty exempts public bodies that operate "services of public interest" from EU rules barring non-competitive behaviour if those rules would hinder them from performing the tasks that have been assigned to them by law.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"State aid - Public undertaking - Combined application of article 92 and article90(2) of the EC Treaty"
Federation francaise des Societes d'Assurances (FFSA) et al
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
supported by the French Republic and La Poste, interveners
application for annulment of the Commission decision of 8 February 1995, published in the OJ of 7 October 1995 (OJ C 262, p. 11)
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
2. Orders the applicants to pay the costs of the proceedings, incuding the cost incurred by the intervener La Poste;
3. Orders the French Republic to bear its own costs.
